info.name: Wire API - Idempotency Test Scenarios
info.description: Senior .NET interview practice collection for idempotency, concurrency, failure recovery, financial validation, and state-transition testing. Import this collection and set the baseUrl environment variable. The current API implements POST /api/wires only; preparation-only scenarios are explicitly marked where an endpoint or failure hook does not exist yet.

item.name: 1. Basic Idempotency
item.description: Run these requests in order. SQL Server check: TEST-001 should occur once in IdempotencyRecords and its WireRequestId should point to exactly one completed WireRequests row.

request.description: Scenario: first use of TEST-001. Observe HTTP 200, a WireRequestId, and Completed status. This proves the business transaction and idempotency record are created. In SQL Server verify one wire and one idempotency row.

exec: pm.test('Status is Completed', function () { pm.expect(body.Status || body.status).to.eql('Completed'); });
pm.test('Response time is under 2 seconds', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.responseTime).to.be.below(2000); });

request.description: Scenario: retry the same logical request. Observe 200 and the same WireRequestId, with no new wire. This is the core financial idempotency guarantee: network retries must not transfer funds twice.

exec: pm.test('Previous-result message is returned', function () { pm.expect(body.Message || body.message).to.eql('Returning previous result.'); });

request.description: Scenario: run this request 3 or more times with Collection Runner. Every response should be 200 and return firstWireId. SQL Server should still contain one TEST-001 idempotency row and one linked wire.

exec: pm.test('No different wire is returned', function () { pm.expect(String(body.WireRequestId || body.wireRequestId)).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('firstWireId')); });

item.name: 2. Idempotency Key Validation
item.description: Missing and empty keys should be rejected before any database write. TEST-002 creates a separate logical operation; reusing TEST-001 with a changed payload must be a conflict.

request.description: Scenario: no idempotency header. Expected 400 Bad Request and no WireRequests or IdempotencyRecords row.

exec: pm.test('No successful wire ID is returned', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.match(/WireRequestId|wireRequestId/); });

request.description: Scenario: blank key. Expected 400 Bad Request, no successful wire ID, and no database rows.

exec: pm.test('No successful wire ID is returned', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.match(/WireRequestId|wireRequestId/); });

request.description: Scenario: new key and new amount. Expected 200 and a new wire. A new idempotency key represents a different logical operation.
Scenario: TEST-001 is reused with amount 90000. Expected 409 Conflict and no second wire. RequestHash detects accidental key reuse that could otherwise alter a financial transfer.

exec: pm.test('No successful wire ID is returned', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.match(/WireRequestId|wireRequestId/); });

item.name: 3. Different Keys
item.description: The same payload under different keys is intentionally treated as a new operation. Verify each key has its own idempotency row and wire.

request.description: Expected 200 and a new WireRequestId different from firstWireId. Different keys mean different logical operations.

exec: pm.test('Wire is different from TEST-001', function () { pm.expect(id).to.not.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('firstWireId')); });

request.description: Expected 200 and another new wire for 100000 USD. Verify RequestHash and business amount in SQL Server.

item.name: 4. Processing State
item.description: Preparation: pause after the first SaveChangesAsync or insert an IdempotencyRecords row manually with Key PROCESSING-001, matching RequestHash, Status Processing, and no completed timestamp. Then run request 10. Current API returns 409 for Processing. For FAILED status, current code treats any non-Processing status as completed and returns 200 with that status; this behavior should be improved before production.

request.description: Requires database preparation described in the folder. Expected 409 Conflict, no new wire, and the existing Processing record remains unchanged.

exec: pm.test('No successful wire ID is returned', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.match(/WireRequestId|wireRequestId/); });

request.description: Expected 200 with the previous WireRequestId and Completed status. This is safe recovery after a client timeout.

exec: pm.test('Previous wire is returned', function () { pm.expect(String(body.WireRequestId || body.wireRequestId)).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('firstWireId')); });

request.description: Requires a manually prepared IdempotencyRecords row with Status Failed and matching RequestHash. Current implementation returns 200 with Status Failed and does not retry; observe and document this explicitly. Desired production behavior should be a defined retry or terminal failure policy.

exec: pm.test('Current implementation returns 200 for non-Processing state', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });

item.name: 5. Database Uniqueness / Race Condition
item.description: Postman does not make a normal collection run concurrent. Open request 13 in two tabs and click Send at the same time, or use Collection Runner with 3 iterations only if your runner/version supports parallel runs. For a deterministic load, use Newman or a small Task.WhenAll client. Verify exactly one wire and one IdempotencyRecord for the key. The current controller can expose a 500 on a unique-key race because it does not catch DbUpdateException; that is a useful interview finding to fix.

request.description: Send this exact request twice concurrently. Expected: one 200 and one 200/409, never two wires. SQL Server unique index on IdempotencyRecords.Key must allow only one record.

exec: pm.test('Concurrency result is success or conflict', function () { pm.expect([200, 409]).to.include(pm.response.code); });
if (pm.response.code === 200) { const body = pm.response.json(); pm.collectionVariables.set('lastWireId', String(body.WireRequestId || body.wireRequestId)); }

request.description: Send 3+ copies simultaneously using the same key and body. Expected exactly one wire. Run by duplicating this request into separate tabs or with Newman/client parallelism.

exec: pm.test('Response is not a successful duplicate creation signal', function () { pm.expect([200, 409]).to.include(pm.response.code); });

item.name: 15. Concurrent same key, different payload A

request.description: Send concurrently with request 15B. Exactly one logical request may win; the other must be 409 (or a documented race-safe result), and only one wire may exist.

exec: pm.test('Expected success or conflict', function () { pm.expect([200, 409]).to.include(pm.response.code); });

item.name: 15B. Concurrent same key, different payload B

request.description: Run concurrently with request 15A. RequestHash protects against two amounts using one key. Verify one IdempotencyRecord and at most one wire.

exec: pm.test('Expected success or conflict', function () { pm.expect([200, 409]).to.include(pm.response.code); });

item.name: 6. Failure Scenarios
item.description: The current API has no development-only failure flag and completes synchronously. These are preparation notes, not executable invented endpoints. Add a Development-only hook or injectable processor before running them.

item.name: 16. Failure after idempotency record creation
item.description: REQUIRES IMPLEMENTATION. Suggested development-only mechanism: a config flag or injected test processor that throws after the first SaveChangesAsync and before completion. Do not expose this in production. Prepare a Processing row, call POST, expect a non-Completed state, then retry and verify the recovery policy. SQL Server: the record must not claim Completed when the wire was not completed.

item.name: 17. Failure after wire creation before HTTP response
item.description: REQUIRES IMPLEMENTATION. Suggested development-only mechanism: throw after both entities are completed but immediately before returning HTTP response. Retry the same key and expect the existing WireRequestId, never a second wire. This models a client timeout after commit.

item.name: 7. Financial Transaction Scenarios
item.description: The current DTO has no validation attributes, so these expected 400/422 tests are likely to fail by creating Completed wires. That failure is intentional evidence for the interview exercise: add validation before treating these as production-safe.

request.description: Expected 400 or 422 and no wire. Zero-value transfers should be rejected before persistence.

exec: pm.test('Invalid amount is rejected', function () { pm.expect([400, 422]).to.include(pm.response.code); });
pm.test('No wire ID is returned', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.match(/WireRequestId|wireRequestId/); });

request.description: Expected 400 or 422 and no wire. Negative money must never enter the transaction ledger.

exec: pm.test('Invalid amount is rejected', function () { pm.expect([400, 422]).to.include(pm.response.code); });

request.description: Expected 400 or 422 and no wire. Sender account is mandatory for auditability and settlement.

exec: pm.test('Missing sender is rejected', function () { pm.expect([400, 422]).to.include(pm.response.code); });

request.description: Expected 400 or 422 and no wire. Recipient account is mandatory.

exec: pm.test('Missing recipient is rejected', function () { pm.expect([400, 422]).to.include(pm.response.code); });

request.description: Expected 400 or 422 and no wire. Self-transfers should be explicitly governed by business rules.

exec: pm.test('Self-transfer policy is enforced', function () { pm.expect([400, 422]).to.include(pm.response.code); });

request.description: Expected 400 or 422 and no wire. Currency should be restricted to supported ISO codes.

exec: pm.test('Currency policy is enforced', function () { pm.expect([400, 422]).to.include(pm.response.code); });

request.description: Expected 400 or 422 and no wire, unless this limit is explicitly supported. Large-value transfers require limits and additional controls.

exec: pm.test('Amount limit is enforced', function () { pm.expect([400, 422]).to.include(pm.response.code); });

request.description: Expected 200 only if the domain supports cents; otherwise 400/422. Verify decimal precision is preserved in SQL Server.

exec: pm.test('Decimal policy returns an intentional status', function () { pm.expect([200, 400, 422]).to.include(pm.response.code); });
if (pm.response.code >= 400) pm.test('Rejected response has no wire ID', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.match(/WireRequestId|wireRequestId/); });

item.name: 8. Approval Workflow
item.description: REQUIRES IMPLEMENTATION. The current API has no approval, rejection, or GET endpoint, so no executable URLs are invented here. Suggested endpoints: POST /api/wires/{id}/approve, POST /api/wires/{id}/reject, GET /api/wires/{id}. Add optimistic concurrency using a rowversion/ETag or equivalent before running these scenarios.

item.name: 26. Approve valid Submitted wire
item.description: REQUIRES IMPLEMENTATION. Suggested endpoint: POST /api/wires/{{approvalWireId}}/approve. Expected 200 and one transition Submitted -> Approved.

item.name: 27. Approve same wire twice
item.description: REQUIRES IMPLEMENTATION. Expected second request to be rejected, not a second approval event.

item.name: 28. Two users approve concurrently
item.description: REQUIRES IMPLEMENTATION. Send two approve requests simultaneously. Exactly one should transition the row; the other should receive a conflict based on concurrency control.

item.name: 29. Approve Completed wire
item.description: REQUIRES IMPLEMENTATION. Expected invalid state transition response, typically 409 Conflict.

item.name: 30. Approve Rejected wire
item.description: REQUIRES IMPLEMENTATION. Expected invalid state transition response, typically 409 Conflict.

item.name: 31. Reject Approved wire
item.description: REQUIRES IMPLEMENTATION. Expected invalid state transition response, typically 409 Conflict.

item.name: 9. GET / Verification
item.description: REQUIRES IMPLEMENTATION. The current API exposes no GET endpoint. Suggested endpoint: GET /api/wires/{id}. These checks should verify the wire status, the single wire per idempotency key, and the IdempotencyRecord relationship. Consider a separate admin-only endpoint for idempotency records rather than exposing internal hashes publicly.

item.name: 32. GET created wire by ID
item.description: REQUIRES IMPLEMENTATION. Suggested request: GET {{baseUrl}}/api/wires/{{firstWireId}}. Expected 200.

item.name: 33. Verify status
item.description: REQUIRES IMPLEMENTATION. Assert the returned wire status is Completed for firstWireId.

item.name: 34. Verify one wire per idempotency key
item.description: DATABASE CHECK. Query IdempotencyRecords by Key = TEST-001 and join to WireRequests. Expected one record and one linked wire.

item.name: 35. Verify idempotency record relationship
item.description: DATABASE CHECK. Verify WireRequestId is populated, RequestHash is stable across retries, and CreatedAt/CompletedAt are populated in the expected order.

item.name: 10. Postman Test Scripts
item.description: The executable requests include status, response ID, status, response-time, and idempotency assertions where applicable. Collection variables firstWireId, test002WireId, test003WireId, and test004WireId are populated by their first requests. Run the Basic Idempotency folder in order before retry assertions.

item.name: Script reference - capture and compare WireRequestId
item.description: Capture: const body = pm.response.json(); pm.collectionVariables.set('firstWireId', String(body.WireRequestId || body.wireRequestId)); Compare retries with pm.expect(String(body.WireRequestId || body.wireRequestId)).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('firstWireId')).

item.name: Script reference - reject invalid writes
item.description: For validation requests assert 400/422 and assert the response does not contain WireRequestId. Follow with SQL verification because an HTTP rejection alone does not prove no row was written.

item.name: Script reference - concurrency result
item.description: For parallel calls accept only 200 or 409 while SQL Server is the source of truth for exactly one IdempotencyRecord and one WireRequest. A 500 during a race is a defect to fix, not a passing result.

item.name: 11. Database Verification Notes
item.description: Run these queries in SQL Server Management Studio against IdempotencyDb. Replace literals as needed. Never expose RequestHash or internal idempotency records through an unauthenticated public API.

item.name: SQL - inspect wires
item.description:
SELECT * FROM WireRequests ORDER BY Id DESC;

Verify: one row per successful logical operation, correct accounts/amount/currency, Completed status, and CompletedAt populated.

item.name: SQL - inspect idempotency records
item.description:
SELECT * FROM IdempotencyRecords ORDER BY Id DESC;

Verify: Key is unique, RequestHash is stable for exact retries, Status transitions correctly, Response is stored only after completion, and timestamps are populated.

item.name: SQL - verify one key and relationship
item.description:
SELECT i.Key, i.RequestHash, i.Status AS IdempotencyStatus, i.WireRequestId, w.Id AS WireId, w.Status AS WireStatus, w.Amount
FROM IdempotencyRecords i
LEFT JOIN WireRequests w ON w.Id = i.WireRequestId
WHERE i.Key = 'TEST-001';

Expected: one idempotency row, one matching wire, and WireRequestId = WireId.

item.name: SQL - find duplicate keys
item.description:
SELECT [Key], COUNT(*) AS RecordCount
FROM IdempotencyRecords
GROUP BY [Key]
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

Expected: zero rows. The unique index is the database backstop for race conditions.

item.name: SQL - find duplicate logical wires
item.description:
SELECT i.[Key], COUNT(w.Id) AS LinkedWireCount
FROM IdempotencyRecords i
LEFT JOIN WireRequests w ON w.Id = i.WireRequestId
GROUP BY i.[Key]
HAVING COUNT(w.Id) > 1;

Expected: zero rows. Also inspect concurrent test keys directly.

item.name: SQL - prepare Processing test record
SQL - prepare Failed test record
item.description: Preparation only. Insert a matching RequestHash with [Status] = 'Failed' and observe request 12. The current controller treats Failed as completed and returns it; define and implement the desired retry policy before relying on this behavior.
